pairs.why: B keeps a related blue/teal field with a cool steel truss and only yellow/red as lamp accents, while A adds yellow end-caps and trim, which brings in an extra loud hue family that the real card doesn't have.
A keeps to the real card's red-orange background, peach floor and green chair with grey legs, while B adds orange armrests that make a fourth hue competing with the hero.
B's purple background is a cooler field behind the gold, closer to the real cards' blue, cyan and orange rays, while A's green is a hue the real cards don't use. The gap is small.
Both ropes use the same purple background and golden-orange hero, and the red tie, shadow color and chroma are nearly identical.
A's green is darker and more olive, and it has a deeper vignette like the real card's green wall, while B's bright lime bricks and extra props (gold cans, striped ball) add louder hues.
B has the real card's yellow glow in the center and a deeper, richer blue bottle, while A's lighter cyan-blue bottle sits on a more orange-heavy ray background.
A keeps more of the real cards' clear blue sky and clean saturated red, while B's dusty tan, grey and orange desert pulls the whole card warmer and more muted.
A gives more of the card to rich teal water against orange wood and a red ring, as the real card does, while B spends more of the card on pale sky blue.
